gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_775/slip: On 18 October 2023, at meeting S/PV.9442, the Security Council considered draft S/2023/775, a separate Russian amendment to the Brazilian draft on the Middle East. The chair counted six votes in favour, one against, and eight abstentions. This tally fell short of the required threshold, preventing adoption. The negative vote by a permanent member further ensured the amendment created no new Council authority.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_775/matched: Russia proposed amendment S/2023/775 to the Brazilian draft, inserting a paragraph after operative paragraph 2. The text condemned indiscriminate attacks on civilians and civilian objects in Gaza, specifically referencing the strike on Al Ahli hospital without inferring a perpetrator, and rejected blockade steps depriving civilians of essentials. The tally was six votes in favour, one against, and eight abstentions, falling short of the required threshold for adoption.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_776/slip: The Security Council separately considered Russian amendment S/2023/776 at meeting S/PV.9442 on 18 October 2023. The tally was seven votes in favour, one against, and seven abstentions. This result fell short of the required threshold for adoption. Consequently, the amendment failed to create new Council authority, mirroring the outcome of the primary Brazilian draft which also failed due to a permanent member's negative vote.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_776/matched: On 18 October 2023, Russia proposed amendment S/2023/776 to Brazil's draft. It inserted an operative paragraph before paragraph 1, calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire that would endure and be fully observed. The chair counted seven votes in favour, one against, and seven abstentions. This tally fell short of the required threshold, preventing adoption. Consequently, the Russian proposal was not incorporated into the final text.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.draft_aid/slip: On 18 October 2023, the Security Council considered Brazil's draft S/2023/773 regarding the Middle East. The draft received twelve votes in favour, one against (United States), and two abstentions (Russia, United Kingdom). The negative vote by a permanent member prevented adoption. Consequently, the proposed aid provisions remained draft language, creating no new Council authority.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.draft_aid/matched: Brazil's draft S/2023/773, submitted on 18 October 2023, proposed aid provisions in operative paragraph 7. These included humanitarian pauses for full, rapid, safe, and unhindered access by UN agencies, the ICRC, and other impartial organizations, alongside encouragement for corridors. The draft received twelve votes in favor, one against (United States), and two abstentions (Russia, United Kingdom). The negative vote by a permanent member prevented adoption, leaving the provisions as draft language without new Council authority.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.veto_explanation/slip: The U.S. representative explained its negative vote on draft S/2023/773 at meeting S/PV.9442 on 18 October 2023. This vote, alongside Russia's and the U.K.'s abstentions, resulted in the draft's non-adoption due to a permanent member's veto. Consequently, no new Council authority was created. The explanation specifically addresses the U.S. position on the main draft, distinct from the separate Russian amendments considered earlier.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.veto_explanation/matched: At meeting S/PV.9442 on 18 October 2023, U.S. representative Linda Thomas-Greenfield explained the United States' negative vote on draft S/2023/773. She objected to the draft's omission of Israel's right of self-defence, citing Article 51 of the UN Charter. Thomas-Greenfield argued the Council should have reaffirmed this right in the text. Her explanation was recorded as the sole rationale for the U.S. vote; no reasons were provided for the abstentions by Russia or the United Kingdom.
